statement.excerpt: Combined with mandates to “use as much AI as possible,” this naturally increases the cost of having software engineers, which — and I say this not wanting anyone to lose their jobs — does the literal opposite of replacing workers with AI.

from_speaker: mandates to “use as much AI as possible”
increases the cost of having software engineers
the literal opposite of replacing workers with AI
I’ve yet to be able to confirm it
our_interpretation: The claim depends on the preceding, explicitly unconfirmed report of compulsory migration from subscriptions to API billing.
The plain reading is that this combination raises employers’ total cost per employed engineer, including tools, without corresponding labor replacement.
Higher token expenditure alone does not establish higher total engineering costs. Subscription savings, staffing changes, and other displaced expenses must also be considered.
This is a conditional causal assertion, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish compulsory billing migration and usage mandates at the same employers, followed by higher comparable costs per engineer attributable to those changes, without offsetting labor replacement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that the combination does not increase costs per engineer, or that offsetting labor replacement defeats the claimed implication.
